content: The document titled Target Product Profiles for Tuberculosis Diagnosis and Detection of Drug Resistance was published by the World Health Organization (WHO) in 2024. It outlines the technical and operational specifications for diagnostic tools aimed at improving the detection of tuberculosis (TB) and drug resistance. The publication is available in both electronic and print formats, with respective ISBNs 978-92-4-009769-8 and 978-92-4-009770-4. The content is distributed under a Creative Commons license, allowing for non-commercial use, adaptation, and redistribution, provided proper citation is given. However, the use of the WHO logo is prohibited, and any adaptations must be licensed under the same or an equivalent Creative Commons license. Translations of the document must include a disclaimer stating that WHO is not responsible for the accuracy or content of the translation, and the original English version remains the authoritative edition. The document was developed by WHO’s Global Tuberculosis Programme with contributions from experts in public health policy, TB program management, and TB diagnosis and care. The development was led by Nazir Ismail, with support from Alexei Korobitsyn and Lice González-Angulo, under the guidance of Matteo Zignol and the overall direction of Tereza Kasaeva, Director of WHO’s Global Tuberculosis Programme. The updated components related to target product profiles (TPPs) for rapid diagnostic tests to detect pulmonary TB at the peripheral level were informed by input from the Scientific TPP Development Group, which included professionals from various countries and organizations. The document acknowledges the contributions of numerous experts, institutions, and stakeholders who participated in consultations, modeling work, and public comment processes. These efforts were supported by funding from the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) and the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation. The TPPs aim to guide the development of innovative diagnostic tools to address critical public health needs, including the detection of TB and drug resistance. The document highlights the importance of updating TPPs to reflect advancements in technology, evolving public health needs, and WHO’s strategic priorities, such as the End TB Strategy and universal health coverage goals. The updated TPPs include definitions for point-of-care (POC) and near-POC tests, emphasizing their suitability for use in low-resource settings without requiring extensive infrastructure or specialized skills. The rapid diagnostic TPP does not differentiate between sputum-based and non-sputum-based tests, as long as the diagnostic tool meets the required targets. The updated TPPs also incorporate a model-based approach to evaluate the performance and cost-effectiveness of new diagnostic tests. This marks the first time such an approach has been used in WHO’s TB diagnostic TPP development process. The revisions were informed by extensive stakeholder engagement, including Delphi consultation processes, public calls for input, and expert meetings. Key changes include expanded testing priorities, inclusive target populations, revised sample types, and considerations for time-to-result linked to treatment decisions. The document concludes with the expectation that these revisions will guide stakeholders involved in TB diagnostics development, including manufacturers, academic institutions, funding agencies, and other partners. The ultimate goal is to enhance TB case identification, improve drug resistance detection, and support timely treatment initiation, thereby contributing to global efforts to combat TB.
